summary: The bill amends DC law to allow police to pursue fleeing suspects in vehicles unless an officer reasonably believes the pursuit would risk harm to bystanders, prove futile, or be less effective than other means, while also requiring a DOJ report on public-alert technology for pursuits.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal or local budgets, appropriations, or expenditures. It focuses solely on amending DC police pursuit rules and requiring a DOJ evaluation report.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the bill.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not mention immigration, border policy, or related enforcement.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No military, defense, or national security spending provisions.
The bill has no environmental or climate-related measures.
No welfare, benefits, or social services provisions.
No education policy, school funding, or choice provisions.
The bill does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.

The bill directly amends DC law to remove multiple prior restrictions on police vehicular pursuits, allowing pursuits unless specific risk or futility conditions are met. This reverses elements of the 2022 justice reform act and expands law enforcement discretion in pursuit tactics, aligning with tougher policing approaches rather than reform-oriented limits.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No deficit, debt, or fiscal policy content.
No provisions affecting LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid or international assistance measures.
No voting rights, election integrity, or electoral reform content.
The bill requires a DOJ report evaluating PursuitAlert technology for public alerts during pursuits, but this is a narrow, one-time evaluation with no regulatory changes to tech or privacy policy.
No labor, union, or workplace provisions.
No religious liberty, civil rights, or anti-discrimination provisions.
